Adjusts the density of the trees. Higher settings mean more trees being rendered on screen, which can reduce performance.
\nNo Trees: No trees will be rendered.
\nLow: Approximately 10% of the trees will be rendered.
\nMedium: Approximately 50% of the trees will be rendered.
Adjusts the quality and view distance of shadows. Shadow quality can have a performance impact on both CPU and GPU performance.
\nOff: Shadows are disabled entirely. This has an obvious impact on visual quality, but it can improve performance on devices that struggle to reach playable framerates.
\nLow: Shadows are lower quality and have a short view distance.
\nMedium: Shadow quality and view distance tries to strike a decent balance between high and low quality.
\nHigh: Shadows are higher quality and have a larger view distance than the lower qualities.
\nVery High: Shadows are at their highest quality and the shadow view distance is dynamic, allowing for far greater shadow view distances when flying.
Adjusts the quality of the water. This can impact visual effects as well as some physics effects.
\nLow: Similar to medium quality without a few effects such as river flows, dynamic waves, and caustics
\nMedium: Water will be rendered with all its various visual and physical effects fully enabled.
\nHigh: Water will be rendered with all its various visual and physical effects fully enabled with increased detail at further distances.
Adjusts the visual quality of the clouds, sky, and fog. Higher settings are very GPU heavy. Lowering this setting can have big performance gains for GPU limited situations.
\nLow: Flat 2D clouds will be used as part of the skybox instead of 3D volumetric clouds.
\nMedium: Volumetric clouds will be used at a reduced quality level.
\nHigh: High quality volumetric clouds will be used.
Adjusts the visual quality of the terrain's surface. Higher settings are very GPU heavy. Lowering this setting can have big performance gains for GPU limited situations.
\nLow: The visual quality of the terrain surface will be significantly reduced.
\nMedium: The visual quality of the terrain surface will be somewhat reduced.
\nHigh: The visual quality of the terrain surface will be at its highest quality.
\nMSAA x2: MSAA 2x (Multi-Sample Anti-Aliasing) samples 2 points per pixel for high-quality edges, but with a higher performance cost.
\nMSAA 4x: MSAA 4x (Multi-Sample Anti-Aliasing) samples 4 points per pixel for high-quality edges, but with a higher performance cost.
\nMSAA 8x: MSAA 8x (Multi-Sample Anti-Aliasing) samples 8 points per pixel for high-quality edges, but with a higher performance cost.
\nFXAA: FXAA (Fast Approximate Anti-Aliasing) quickly smooths edges with a slight blur, offering high performance but lower visual quality.
\nSMAA: SMAA (Subpixel Morphological Anti-Aliasing) reduces jagged edges with minimal performance impact, providing a good balance between quality and performance.
Defines the frequency of the foam simulation on the water surface.
\nLow: Water will simulate foam at a lower frequency.
\nMedium: Water will simulate foam at a moderate frequency.
\nHigh: Water will simulate foam at a higher frequency.
This setting changes the way reflections are handled on the craft surfaces.
\nRealtime: Reflective craft parts will reflect the surrounding world in realtime. Enabling this option can result in extreme performance impacts.
\nStatic: Reflective craft parts will use a vague static image to give the illusion of the parts reflecting their surroundings without actually doing so.
This value scales the rendered resolution of the game while the user interface still renders at the specified resolution.
\nAt values lower than 1, the game will be rendered at a lower resolution than the game screen and then upscaled. This is a trade-off of reduced graphical quality for performance gains.

\nAt values higher than 1, the game will be rendered at a higher resolution than the game screen and then downscaled. This is a trade-off of increased graphical quality (particularly a reduction in aliasing) at the cost of performance.
Toggles the waves along the shorelines. This has minimal impact on performance but some players may prefer less turbulent shorelines, either for physics-related or perhaps just visual reasons.
